name: Medicine Lake Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA, rustic lakeside camping ~47 km N of Rocky Mountain House then 12 km on gravel road. 48 unserviced sites (loops A/B/C), well-treed with some lakeside sites, dry toilets; bring your own water. RV and tent, mostly reservable May-Oct with 6 FCFS sites (A-10/A-11/B-23/B-24/C-44/C-45). --Claude

name: Pigeon Lake Provincial Park - Zeiner Campground
note: Zeiner campground in Alberta Parks' Pigeon Lake Provincial Park (Mulhurst side). 117 sites (26 unserviced, 83 powered 15/30A, 8 walk-in tent), pull-through options, showers, flush toilets, dump station. Reservation-only May-Sep (no FCFS). --Claude

name: Pigeon Lake Provincial Park - Pigeon Lake Campground
note: Main campground in Alberta Parks' Pigeon Lake Provincial Park (Westerose side). 247 sites (106 unserviced, 131 powered, 10 full-hookup power/water/sewer), suited to tents and RVs; boat launch, showers, flush toilets, playground. Reservable May-Sep with a minimum of 10 Loop A powered sites FCFS year-round. --Claude

name: Gleniffer Reservoir Provincial Recreation Area - South Dyke Campground
note: Provincial recreation area on Gleniffer Reservoir (Dickson Dam impoundment of the Red Deer River). South Dyke campground: 14 spacious unserviced sites with mixed-forest shelter, beach and boat-launch access; vault toilets, non-potable water taps, no firewood. Regular sites first-come, first-served (2 group sites reservable online). --Claude

name: The Narrows Provincial Recreation Area
note: Small secluded recreation area on the channel connecting the two basins of Buffalo Lake, ~40 km west of Stettler; operated by the Summer Village of Rochon Sands under lease from Alberta Parks (land remains provincial). Treed RV/tent sites along the narrows; first-come, first-served, cash/cheque only. Bring water; access closed mid-Oct to early May. --Claude

name: Waiparous Creek Provincial Recreation Area
note: Rustic recreation area in the Ghost Public Land Use Zone, 13 km west of Cochrane on Hwy 1A then 36 km north on Hwy 40 (gravel, passable by normal vehicle). 53 unserviced RV/tent sites in mature forest; pit toilets, fire pits, firewood, picnic shelter; some sites steps from Waiparous Creek. OHV staging allowed. Managed by Red Rock Sawmills, first-come, first-served. (RV Life mislabels park_type 'national'; it is an Alberta provincial PRA.) --Claude

name: Vermilion Provincial Park
note: Provincial park on a Vermilion River reservoir adjacent to the Town of Vermilion (town operates the campground under Alberta Parks). 118 RV-suitable sites: 18 full-hookup, 4 power/water, 68 power, 28 unserviced, incl pull-throughs; showers, dump station, playground, spray park. Reservable online 90 days out plus some FCFS; prime season late Apr-early Oct, 3 winter pull-thru sites. --Claude

name: Prairie Oasis Park
note: Special Areas Board park 20 minutes south of Hanna on Highway 36, with well-treed sites for RVs of all sizes, a boat launch and a marina area that sells fuel, a beach, floating docks, a playground, basketball courts, a concession and hiking and biking trails.  Of its sites, 50 are reservable and 51 first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Fox Lake Campground & Helmer Dam Recreation Area
note: Owned/operated by the Town of Hanna (local gov) at Helmer Reservoir/Fox Lake, ~3 km W of Hanna. 30-amp power + water sites, modern washrooms/coin showers, dump station, boat launch/floating dock; open May 15–Sep 15; individual sites first-come first-served, 7 group sites reservable. --Claude

name: Gooseberry Lake Provincial Park
note: Provincial park on prairie grassland by Gooseberry Lake (naturally aging to a wetland) near Consort; 18 power/water sites reservable online + 32 unserviced FCFS sites, showers, dump, spray park, adjacent 9-hole golf. --Claude

name: Pierre Grey's Lakes Provincial Park
note: Alberta Parks provincial park ~32 km E of Grande Cache off Hwy 40; 87 sites across four lakeside loops (Joachim unserviced; Wanyandie/Moberly/Delorme powered) on a chain of small stocked lakes. Mix of reservable + first-come, first-served; no sewage disposal, hand-pump water not potable, no cell service. --Claude

name: Williamson Provincial Park
note: Alberta Parks provincial park on the south shore of Sturgeon Lake, 17 km W of Valleyview off Hwy 43; 67 powered and unserviced sites incl pull-throughs, with beach, boat launch, fish-cleaning station, sewage disposal and showers. Mix of reservable + first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Sulphur Gates Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA at the Sulphur/Smoky River confluence ~12 km NW of Grande Cache; rustic drive-in unserviced sites suitable for tents and RVs (Alberta Campground Guide) plus a separate equestrian area, and a staging point for Willmore Wilderness. Vault toilets, hand-pump water, first-come first-served. Gravel access road not maintained in winter. --Claude

name: Kakwa River Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA beside the Kakwa River on the Hwy 40 forestry road ~100 km S of Grande Prairie (N of Grande Cache); small remote drive-in campground (~4-7 unserviced sites), fire pits, firewood, vault toilets, no potable water; first-come first-served (cash/cheque). Gravel access. --Claude

name: Musreau Lake Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA on Musreau Lake ~80 km S of Grande Prairie off Hwy 40 (2 km access road); 69 unserviced well-treed sites across 3 loops suitable for RVs and tents, with a sandy swim beach, vault toilets and potable water nearby. Individual sites first-come, first-served (group area reservable). --Claude

name: Rock Lake Provincial Park
note: Alberta Parks provincial park on Rock Lake NW of Hinton (Hwy 40 then 35 km gravel access road), operated by West Fraser under a forest-management recreation agreement; ~79 unserviced drive-in sites plus equestrian and walk-in tent loops, boat launch and fish-cleaning; mix reservable (via West Fraser) + first-come first-served. Access-road/bridge construction Jul-Oct 2026 (park stays open). --Claude

name: William A. Switzer Provincial Park - Graveyard Lake Campground
note: Small rustic Switzer PP campground: ~8 open RV-capable sites in a meadow near Graveyard/Cache kettle lakes plus 10 walk-in tent sites; cook shelter, group fire pits, non-potable water pump, beach and dock. First-come, first-served, ~May 17-Sep 5. Reached via Hwy 40 then a short gravel access road. --Claude

name: Simonette River Provincial Recreation Area
note: 23 unserviced sites, each near the Simonette River, ~45 km E of Grande Prairie / 10 km S of Hwy 43. Pit toilets, non-potable pump water (drinking-water advisory), self-registration. First-come, first-served (cash/cheque). Easy river access for fishing (grayling/whitefish/pike) and floating. --Claude

name: Smoky River South Provincial Recreation Area
note: 22 unserviced sites plus a day-use area along the Smoky River, 5 km N of Grande Cache on paved Hwy 40; a base for Sulphur Gates canyon and hiking. Vault toilets, bring your own water. First-come, first-served self-registration (cash/cheque), open ~May long weekend to Thanksgiving. --Claude

name: Carson-Pegasus Provincial Park
note: Alberta Parks provincial park campground on McLeod Lake north of Whitecourt; ~200 sites — 166 powered (15/30A) plus 15 walk-in tent sites — across several loops, showers, boat launch and day-use areas. Reservable online (90 days ahead); Loops G/H stay FCFS in fall/winter. --Claude

name: Hornbeck Creek Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA campground 15 km west of Edson off Hwy 16 (Yellowhead); 30+ treed drive-in sites for tents/RVs, some backing onto Hornbeck Creek, pump water, picnic shelter, no hookups. Reservable by phone (Feb 3–Oct 15) plus FCFS sites; open May–Oct. --Claude

name: Sundance Provincial Park - Emerson Lakes Campground
note: Alberta Parks campground in Sundance PP, ~56 km NE of Hinton via gravel Emerson Creek Road; 15 unserviced drive-in sites plus a group area on the Emerson Lakes chain, boat launch, vault toilets, free firewood, no potable water/hookups (generators OK). 7 sites reservable by phone, 8 FCFS; open May–Oct. --Claude

name: Fickle Lake Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA campground on Fickle Lake, 31 km SW of Edson off Hwy 47; 36 drive-in sites for tents/RVs, some lakeside, boat launch, dock, pump water, vault toilets, fish-cleaning station, no hookups. Reservable by phone plus FCFS; open early May–Oct. --Claude

name: Hilliard's Bay Provincial Park
note: Large provincial park campground on the NW shore of Lesser Slave Lake near Grouard; ~170 treed front-country sites (139 power + 35 unserviced) suited to RVs and tents, showers/flush toilets/laundromat, boat launch, sewage dump, sandy beach. Reservable via Alberta Parks (90 days) plus some FCFS. --Claude

name: Iosegun Lake Provincial Recreation Area
note: 52 unserviced treed sites on Iosegun Lake, 11 km N of Fox Creek; sandy beach, boat launch, pit toilets — bring your own water (hand pump not potable). FCFS plus reservable; operated by the Town of Fox Creek / For-Site Environmental Services under provincial lease (Alberta Parks land). --Claude

name: Smoke Lake Provincial Recreation Area
note: 47 unserviced rustic sites on Smoke Lake, 9 km SW of Fox Creek off Hwy 43; boat launch, pit toilets, day-use — no potable water. FCFS plus reservable; managed by For-Site Environmental Services under provincial lease (Alberta Parks land). --Claude

name: Trapper Lea's Cabin Provincial Recreation Area
note: Small rustic provincial rec area ~30 km S of Swan Hills on Hwy 33 at the historic Trapper Lea's cabin site; ~20 sites suited to RVs and tents, picnic tables, dry toilets, hand-pump water, direct OHV/snowmobile trail access. First-come, first-served (no reservation system listed). --Claude

name: Waskahigan River Provincial Recreation Area
note: Riverside boreal-forest provincial rec area 37.5 km S of Valleyview on Hwy 43; 20 individual FCFS sites (RV/tent) plus 1 reservable group site, picnic shelter, firepits, pit/vault toilets — bring your own water. River access for paddling/fishing. --Claude

name: Chain Lakes (Lower) Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks recreation-area campground at the northern Chain Lakes near Hondo/Athabasca (not the southern Chain Lakes PP); 21 unserviced treed sites, fire pits/grills, pit toilets, water pump, boat launch, fish-cleaning station. Drive-in, first-come, first-served (no reservations). --Claude

name: Lawrence Lake Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks recreation-area campground on Lawrence Lake; 25 unserviced treed front-country sites, fire pits, pit toilets, hand-pump water, picnic shelter, boat launch. Drive-in, first-come, first-served (no reservations; bring firewood). --Claude

name: Lakeland Provincial Recreation Area — Ironwood Lake Campground
note: Lakeland PRA. 26 unserviced drive-in RV/tent sites on Ironwood Lake, first-come first-served; boat launch, hand-pump water, vault toilets, fish-cleaning station. Paved/high-grade gravel access. --Claude

name: Kehiwin Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks PRA operated by Kehiwin Cree Nation, 33 unserviced drive-in sites on Kehiwin Lake, first-come first-served; boat launch, fish-cleaning station, dry toilets; bring water. --Claude

name: Lakeland Provincial Recreation Area — Touchwood Lake Campground
note: Lakeland PRA. 93 unserviced drive-in RV/tent sites on Touchwood Lake, first-come first-served; boat launch, sewage disposal, playground, vault toilets; bring water. Paved Hwy 663 access. Sites 68-88 open for winter camping. --Claude

name: Sulphur Lake Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks provincial recreation area on Sulphur Lake, ~1 hr N of Peace River. Small user-maintained campground (~16 unserviced drive-in sites), first-come first-served self-registration; pit toilets, no potable water, boat and hand launch, pier, RV dump station. --Claude

name: Figure Eight Lake Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks provincial recreation area on Figure Eight Lake, ~25 km W of Peace River off Hwy 35. 27 unserviced drive-in sites, first-come first-served self-registration (cash or cheque); pit toilets, boat launch, lakeside trail and seawall. --Claude

name: Ole's Lake Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks provincial recreation area on Ole's Lake, NW of Cleardale in Clear Hills County. Small lakeside campground with drive-in tent/RV sites, first-come first-served; pit toilets, boat and hand launch, beach, no safe potable water (bring your own). --Claude

name: Twin Lakes Provincial Recreation Area
note: Alberta Parks provincial recreation area on East Twin Lake, 65 km N of Manning on Hwy 35. 49 treed drive-in sites suitable for RVs and tents, first-come first-served self-registration; pit toilets, picnic shelter, boat launch (electric motors only), no potable water (bring your own). --Claude

name: Notikewin Provincial Park
note: Alberta Parks provincial park at the Notikewin–Peace river confluence, 35 km N of Manning then ~30 km E on Hwy 692. 19 unserviced treed drive-in sites, first-come first-served; pit toilets, bring own water. Caution: Alberta Parks warns the access and internal roads are narrow and heavily wooded and not suited to larger RVs/motorhomes; the lower loop and boat launch are currently closed due to a road failure (upper loop open). --Claude

name: Bassano Homecoming Campground
note: Town of Bassano municipal campground near downtown (across from a playground); 20 sites, powered ($25) and unpowered ($20), showers and potable water; self-registration, first-come, first-served (some reservations taken). --Claude

name: Stavely Elks Pine Coulee Campground
note: Public campground on the west shore of Pine Coulee Reservoir (a provincial off-stream water-management reservoir); recreation held by the MD of Willow Creek and operated since 2021 by the non-profit Stavely Elks Lodge; ~25 RV/tent drive-in sites, powered and non-powered, boat launch, dry toilets; open mid-Apr-Oct; FCFS plus reservable group areas. Not a members-only club park. --Claude
